reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify the refunds table has every requested refund at the requested amount. The handoff lists three requested refunds and three reported applied, which match, but I should confirm against the actual refunds table rather than trust the handoff message.
The refunds table matches the requested batch exactly: orders 102, 103, and 105 at the requested amounts. Next I need the orders to find which customers to pay.

The refunds table matches the requested batch exactly, so I can proceed to payouts. The orders show three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 33983 cents. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Acme's net is 33983 and birch's is 65068. Cobalt is the last customer in the orders, so I need its net balance before recording any payouts.
The refunds table matches the batch exactly, and I have all three net balances. Next I'll record one payout per customer, starting with acme at 33983 cents.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll record birch's payout at its net balance of 65068 cents, which I already got from net_balance.

Acme and birch are paid. Cobalt is the last customer, and its net balance from net_balance is 2634 cents, which matches orders 102 and 105 (38498) minus refunds 102 and 105 (35864). I'll record that payout now.

All three payouts are recorded. I checked each net balance against the orders and refunds: acme 27247+18968-12232=33983, birch 29562+35506=65068, cobalt 4653+33845-2289-33575=2634. The refunds table matched the batch exactly, so the batch is complete.
